extracted.intended_audience: Prospective and current NIDCD NRSA fellowship applicants (predoctoral and postdoctoral) and their sponsors/mentors
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and requirements for preparing, submitting, and managing NIDCD individual NRSA fellowship (F30/F31/F32) applications, including eligibility, research training plan, sponsor responsibilities, clinical trial rules, submission mechanics, review, resubmission, and post-award administration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinical trial inclusion policy for fellowships
rubrics_metrics.description: Stand-alone independent clinical trials cannot be proposed as part of the research plan in a fellowship application; applicants may gain clinical trial experience only as part of a mentor-led clinical trial or by proposing additional components within the scope of an existing mentor-led trial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The clinical trial must meet the NIH definition and follow NIH clinical trial guidelines (funding source need not be NIH). Options include: being part of the clinical trial team and using generated data; adding an intervention/measures/subpopulation within existing scope; or adding an out-of-scope component only with mentor documentation (IRB approval, mentor statement assuming responsibility and funding, approval by the trial's funding source). For fellowships proposing a clinical trial experience, the sponsor/co-sponsor must include a statement documenting leadership, funding source, ClinicalTrials.gov identifier if applicable, and description of expertise in the Sponsor and Co-Sponsor Statements attachment of the F.430 - PHS Fellowship Supplemental Form. Also note change-of-scope considerations when adding components.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant-authored Research Training Plan
rubrics_metrics.description: The Research Training Plan must be written by the applicant and should describe the collaborative process with the sponsor/co-sponsor in its development, review, and editing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While some similarity to the sponsor's research is expected, the applicant’s Research Training Plan should not duplicate research for which the sponsor/co-sponsor is already receiving funding. The sponsor's role and mentoring contributions should be documented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of correct application form (F30/F31/F32) and Program Announcement
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must use the most recent application form linked from the Program Announcement for the specific fellowship type (e.g., Parent F30, F31, F32).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtain the form via the 'Apply for Grant Electronically' link in the relevant FOA/program announcement to ensure correct form version and attachments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fit to NIDCD scientific scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed research must fall within NIDCD’s strategic plan and research areas and contribute to the Institute's mission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants are strongly encouraged to email the NIDCD Extramural Research Training Officer several months before preparing an application, including an NIH-format biosketch, a one-page description of aims, the study population, and mentor names. After NIDCD evaluates materials, they will advise whether the project fits NIDCD requirements for submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility and program selection for Au.D. students
rubrics_metrics.description: Au.D. students in certain training paths are eligible for specific fellowships (F30, F32, etc.) depending on program type and career stage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If in a combined Au.D./Ph.D. dual-degree program, you can apply for the appropriate F30 variant. If you completed an Au.D. and entered a Ph.D. program in biomedical research supported by NIDCD, consider the F32 Research Dissertation Fellowship for Au.D. Audiologists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendix content restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Appendix materials must comply with NIH appendix policy; clinical trial-related materials are eliminated from the appendix for applications submitted on or after Jan 25, 2018.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to the Updated Appendix Policy Eliminates Clinical Trial-Related Materials and subsequent notices for allowed/disallowed appendix content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable accommodations and budget requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Fellowship applications may request funds to cover interpretive services or other reasonable accommodations for applicants with disabilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include several paragraphs in the application documenting the disability and justifying a specific supplemental budgetary request for the accommodation(s), treating them as reasonable accommodations under the ADA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value of preliminary data and feasibility evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Credible preliminary data related to specific aims, while not required, generally strengthens an application by demonstrating feasibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include feasibility data showing the applicant, sponsor, and/or lab can perform the experiments; published or in-press papers demonstrating access to proposed methods bolster feasibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality of applicant research aims
rubrics_metrics.description: Fellowship applications must present an original research plan authored by the applicant and guided by the sponsor(s); they must not be direct reproductions of the sponsor's funded grant aims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research can be within the sponsor’s area but cannot be a 'cut-and-paste' from the sponsor's research grant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sponsor qualifications and resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Sponsors/mentors need not be NIH-funded but must demonstrate they have the necessary research resources and scientific/technical expertise to effectively mentor the fellow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documentation or statements demonstrating sponsor expertise and available resources are expected in the application materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biosketch listing of manuscripts in preparation/submitted
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants may list manuscripts that are submitted or in preparation on their biosketch; sponsors, co-sponsors, or other significant contributors should not list such manuscripts on their biosketches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow NIH biosketch formatting and content rules when listing unpublished or in-progress works.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsible Conduct of Research (RCR) training requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: NRSA-supported fellows must receive instruction in responsible conduct of research consistent with NIH policy NOT-OD-10-019.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training must occur at least once during each career stage and at a frequency of no less than once every four years. See NOT-OD-10-019 for specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference letter submission mechanics
rubrics_metrics.description: Each reference must submit a letter electronically via eRA Commons using the required reference form as outlined in the Program Announcement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Letters may be submitted any time after the funding opportunity opens and must be complete by the application receipt deadline. Letters submitted early will be held and later linked to the application upon receipt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may not write required reference letters
rubrics_metrics.description: A sponsor or co-sponsor cannot be one of the three required reference letter writers for the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Letters of support from collaborators (e.g., for critical reagents) are separate and belong in Other Attachments; they are not the same as required reference letters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Importance and timing of pre-submission contact with NIDCD
rubrics_metrics.description: Contacting the NIDCD Extramural Research Training Officer several months before the submission deadline is strongly encouraged and important.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include an NIH-format biosketch, one-page aims, study population, and mentor names when requesting assignment or advising on fit to NIDCD.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-submission supplemental materials policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Supplemental/post-submission materials are governed by NIH policies; allowable materials must be received by the NIH Scientific Review Officer (SRO) at least 30 calendar days before the first day of the scheduled review meeting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such information must be sent to the SRO by the Authorized Organization Representative. See Update to the NIH/AHRQ/NIOSH Policy on Post-Submission Materials for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission/Amendment requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A resubmitted/amended application fully supersedes the previous one; no materials are carried forward automatically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must provide new reference letters and all supporting materials with revised applications (you may request the same individuals to re-submit letters). Reviewers will, however, receive the prior summary statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: NRSA employment/time-commitment and outside activities
rubrics_metrics.description: NRSA regulations require a full-time, 40-hours-per-week commitment to the fellowship; limited outside work is allowed only if it does not encroach on research training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: With sponsor and institutional concurrence, NIDCD allows fellowship awardees to accept teaching assistantships involving up to 15-20 hours per week beyond the NRSA commitment.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIDCD review and scoring practices (not percentiled)
rubrics_metrics.description: NIDCD does not percentile fellowship application scores; funding decisions are based on reviewer narrative critiques (summary statement), the raw unnormalized impact/priority score, and available funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIDCD may use a 'not discussed/unscoring' procedure: applications in the lower half may be marked 'not discussed' (no overall impact/priority score), though they still receive written critiques and criteria scores.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria scores, discussion, and overall impact/priority score calculation
rubrics_metrics.description: All applications receive criteria scores from assigned reviewers (1-9 scale). Applications in the top ~50% are discussed and may receive an overall impact/priority score.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The overall impact/priority score is the average of reviewers' overall impact/priority scores multiplied by 10 (e.g., average 2.7 → overall score 27). Criteria scores use the 1-9 NIH scoring scale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for summary statements and score availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Summary statements and review panel scores are made available via NIH Commons; panel scores are entered within three working days after review; summary statements for expedited 'not discussed' processes are normally available two to three weeks after the review meeting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not contact the SRO for scores; SROs will refer you to NIH Commons. Contact Commons Helpdesk for account issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment indicator in application ID
rubrics_metrics.description: An application's NIH application ID number reflects which NIH institute has primary assignment (e.g., 'DC' designator indicates NIDCD).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the application ID or grant number in correspondence to confirm assignment (example format: 1F31DC#####-0).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference letter timing and linkage behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: Reference letters can be submitted before the grant application and will be held until the application is received and then linked; all letters must be complete by the application receipt deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Letters may be submitted any time after the FOA opens but not later than the application due date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-award activation requirements and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Awardees must activate their Notice of Grant Award (NGA) within six months of the award date (cannot activate from Oct 1 through Nov 30) and must complete required forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete and have your Institutional Business Office submit the PHS 416-5 form to activate. For postdoctoral F32 awards, also complete a Payback Agreement form; predoctoral F31 awardees do not have a payback agreement. Forms are in the NIH Grants and Funding Forms Library.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual progress report form requirement (RPPR)
rubrics_metrics.description: Grantees must submit annual progress reports using the Research Performance Progress Report (RPPR).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the RPPR system and guidance to report progress to NIH for fellowship awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Termination procedures and form
rubrics_metrics.description: To terminate a fellowship, complete the Termination Notice form (PHS 416-7).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This form must be submitted by the Institutional Business Office to the NIDCD Grants Management Branch; find the form in the NIH Grants and Funding Forms Library.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stipend levels and supplementation policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Postdoctoral stipends are set by NIH policy; NIDCD allocations follow NIH stipend levels and NIH Grants Policy Statement rules for supplementation of stipends, compensation, and other income.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the NIH Office of Extramural Research FAQs on training and fellowship stipends and the NIH Grants Policy Statement for allowable supplementation rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interaction with institutional offers (e.g., TA) while on fellowship
rubrics_metrics.description: Fellowship holders may accept certain institutional appointments (like TAs) only if such duties do not encroach on the NRSA training commitment and have sponsor plus institutional official concurrence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIDCD allows TAs involving up to 15-20 hours per week beyond the 40-hour NRSA commitment with proper approvals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Where to include program descriptions and letters of support in application
rubrics_metrics.description: Descriptions of graduate/combined degree programs and letters of support from collaborators belong in the Other Attachments section of the application, not as reference letters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differentiate letters of support (Other Attachments) from required reference letters (submitted via eRA Commons). Follow FOA instructions for Other Attachments content and placement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic submission help and contacts
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants experiencing problems with electronic submission should consult NIH Grants and Funding Help resources and contact the Commons Helpdesk as needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commons Helpdesk: 1-866-504-9552; institutional offices (sponsored research, eRA staff) may assist with Commons-related issues.
